5:43 am update, typing one-handed sorry. can you edit this note to my colleague? want it short and professional but not stiff:

"Hi, quick update. I finished the first module of the reassessment-software training, and I have to finish the rest before I come back. I'm returning Monday Jan 5 after adding three weeks of vacation to my leave. First month will be hybrid. Let me know if you need anything from me before then. Thanks!"

Happy to help. Here's a tightened version:

"Hi [colleague's name],

Quick update: I've finished the first module of the reassessment-software training and will complete the remaining modules before I return. I'll be back on Monday, January 5, after adding three weeks of vacation to my leave, and my first month will be hybrid.

If you need anything from me before then, just let me know. Thanks!

[your name]"

I cut the repeated 'I' openings and gave the dates a cleaner shape. If you'd like it warmer, I can add a line like 'Looking forward to getting back into it.'

nice, that works. also the storm cancelled the walk again so we're doing indoor stuff with a four month old. cool cool cool. anyway, can you put the remaining modules in table form with target dates? i'll fill in how many there are, i think better in tables

Sure. Since I don't know how many modules there are or their names, here's a template you can fill in, with dates left for you to set:

| Module | Topic | Est. time | Target date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [topic] | [hours] | [date] | Done |
| 2 | [topic] | [hours] | [date] | Not started |
| 3 | [topic] | [hours] | [date] | Not started |
| 4 | [topic] | [hours] | [date] | Not started |
| Final | Wrap-up / assessment | [hours] | [date before Jan 5] | Not started |

Since the training has to be done before you return, I'd work backward from Monday, January 5 and leave a buffer week at the end. If you tell me the module count and time estimates, I'll fill in the dates. Short nap-sized blocks of 20–30 minutes tend to work well around a baby's schedule too.
